LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School before being selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

### Career Highlights

| Team | Years | Key Achievements |
|------|-------|------------------|
| **Cleveland Cavaliers** | 2003–2010, 2014–2018 | NBA Finals appearances (2007, 2015), MVP awards (2009, 2010) |
| **Miami Heat** | 2010–2014 | Two NBA championships (2012, 2013), Finals MVPs |
| **Los Angeles Lakers** | 2018–present | NBA championship (2020), Finals MVP (2020) |

He has earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards, four NBA Finals MVP awards, and has been named to the All-NBA First Team numerous times. Off the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy—most notably the *I Promise* program, which supports at-risk youth—and his ventures into media and entertainment, including producing films and television shows.

### Legacy

LeBron's impact extends beyond statistics; he's celebrated for his versatility, leadership, and longevity. His influence on the game, culture, and community continues to shape basketball and society at large.
